_comment: Terminology. `terms` was DERIVED from English values that already have more than one Chinese rendering in this catalog, so every entry marks a real inconsistency — but not every inconsistency is an error. `ratified: true` means the variants differ only by punctuation width or whitespace, which is mechanical; `ratified: false` means the same English word is doing different jobs (`Back` is 返回 in a dialog and 上一步 in a wizard) and a reader has to decide whether it is one term or several. `glossary.test.ts` enforces `forbidden` only for ratified entries, so an unratified candidate cannot force a wrong translation.

_openQuestions: Parentheses containing Latin-only content: full-width （Esc） or half-width (Esc)? The catalog currently does both. CLReq prescribes Chinese-style punctuation in principle but carves out formula-heavy scientific text; a UI key hint is arguably neither. Decide, write it into STYLE-zh-CN.md section 1, then ratify the two affected entries.

34 candidates await a reader. Each is one English value with more than one Chinese rendering; ratifying means deciding whether it is one term (forbid the variants) or several (split the keys and remove the entry).
_dntNote: Proper nouns only. Abbreviations such as PR, CR, API, CLI and URL are deliberately absent: they behave as common nouns and inflect — Russian declines 'PR' to 'пул-реквеста', which is correct, not a defect. Matching is word-boundary, not substring, for the same reason.
